description: Defines how A.R.I.A. converts validated case experience into future diagnostic priors, route-performance knowledge, user-specific experience, contextual patterns, and candidate canonical knowledge without corrupting the underlying knowledge graph.

core_principle.statement: ARIA shall learn from validated experience by adjusting future expectations and routing behavior while preserving the distinction between observed history, statistical pattern, technical inference, and canonical truth.
rules: A completed case is not automatically a trustworthy learning example.
Learning strength shall depend on evidence quality, diagnosis quality, causal confidence, validation quality, context completeness, and outcome certainty.
User-specific learning shall remain attributable to the applicable user.
Shared technical learning shall preserve context.
Repeated experience may propose new canonical knowledge but shall not silently promote correlation into truth.
Case history shall remain immutable even when learned aggregates change.

learning_outputs.name: CASE_EXPERIENCE_RECORD
learning_outputs.description: Permanent structured record of what occurred in the completed case.

learning_outputs.name: FAILURE_PRIOR_UPDATE
learning_outputs.description: Adjustment to learned historical frequency for failure modes within applicable context.

learning_outputs.name: ROUTE_PERFORMANCE_UPDATE
learning_outputs.description: Adjustment to learned performance of diagnostic actions and routes.

learning_outputs.name: USER_EXPERIENCE_UPDATE
learning_outputs.description: Contextual learning associated with a specific user's demonstrated observations, actions, outcomes, or recurring patterns.

learning_outputs.name: TEAM_EXPERIENCE_UPDATE
learning_outputs.description: Contextual learning associated with a crew or team when individual attribution is not appropriate.

learning_outputs.name: PRODUCT_EXPERIENCE_UPDATE
learning_outputs.description: Historical learning associated with a product, variant, hardware revision, firmware, topology, or configuration.

learning_outputs.name: MANUFACTURER_EXPERIENCE_UPDATE
learning_outputs.description: Historical learning associated with equipment from an applicable manufacturer.

learning_outputs.name: SYMPTOM_PATTERN_UPDATE
learning_outputs.description: Learning about combinations of symptoms and their relationship to confirmed outcomes.

learning_outputs.name: EVIDENCE_PATTERN_UPDATE
learning_outputs.description: Learning about the diagnostic value of evidence patterns.

learning_outputs.name: CANDIDATE_KNOWLEDGE_CLAIM
learning_outputs.description: Proposed technical knowledge derived from repeated validated experience and routed through the knowledge-governance process.

learning_eligibility_states.name: FULL
learning_eligibility_states.description: Case is sufficiently validated for normal contribution to applicable learned experience.

learning_eligibility_states.name: RESTRICTED
learning_eligibility_states.description: Case contains useful validated information but uncertainty limits which learning targets or weights are appropriate.

learning_eligibility_states.name: ROUTE_ONLY
learning_eligibility_states.description: Case is insufficient to teach root-cause frequency but can still teach diagnostic route performance.

learning_eligibility_states.name: EVIDENCE_ONLY
learning_eligibility_states.description: Case can teach evidence interpretation or measurement patterns but not validated root-cause probability.

learning_eligibility_states.name: USER_ONLY
learning_eligibility_states.description: Case may update a user-specific action or evidence pattern without supporting broader technical generalization.

learning_eligibility_states.name: EXCLUDED
learning_eligibility_states.description: Case shall not modify learned diagnostic aggregates.

rules: Learning confidence shall not exceed what the weakest critical causal factor can reasonably support.
A resolved case with uncertain root cause may have high resolution confidence but low causal learning confidence.
A case with strong root-cause isolation but incomplete long-term validation may contribute causal learning while receiving reduced resolution learning weight.
Exact weighting shall remain configurable and calibratable.

case_weight.description: Each case contributes to learned aggregates according to a bounded learning weight rather than raw count alone.
case_weight.conceptual_formula: case_weight = learning_confidence * context_applicability * attribution_confidence * recency_weight * independence_weight
rules: Fully validated high-quality cases may approach weight 1.0.
Restricted cases shall contribute less than fully validated cases.
Excluded cases contribute 0.
Raw case count shall remain separately available.
The Experience Ledger stores the learning event, not merely the resulting aggregate.
Aggregates shall be reproducible from underlying learning events.
Historical learning events shall not be rewritten when later weighting models change.
New aggregation logic may recalculate current statistics from preserved ledger records.

failure_frequency_learning.description: Validated resolved cases may update the empirical frequency of confirmed failure modes within applicable contexts.
rules: Failure frequency shall be stored as weighted experience, not universal truth.
A case may contribute to multiple contextual aggregates using the same underlying learning event.
Aggregation across dimensions shall not duplicate the case as independent evidence.
Probability calculations shall use effective sample size and regularization.

route_learning.description: ARIA shall learn whether diagnostic actions actually reduced uncertainty, saved time, produced reliable evidence, or contributed to successful resolution.
rules: An action that rules out a hypothesis may be considered successful.
An action that finds the root cause but consumes excessive time may still receive lower routing efficiency than a faster alternative.
Route success and diagnosis correctness are separate learning dimensions.
Route statistics shall preserve context.
Failed routes remain valuable learning data.

user_learning.description: ARIA may learn contextual patterns about how specific users observe, configure, troubleshoot, execute actions, and communicate technical information.
rules: User learning must remain contextual.
ARIA shall not create one universal competence or credibility score.
Reporter identity shall not imply fault attribution.
Improvement over time shall be reflected in learned user experience.
Older user history may receive less predictive weight when newer validated experience indicates change.
User-specific learning may affect priors, routing, evidence requests, and communication style.
User-specific learning shall not override direct validated evidence.
Personal judgment labels shall not be stored as technical learning.

attribution_learning.description: Learning about human actions requires clear attribution of who performed, observed, diagnosed, corrected, and validated relevant technical work.
rules: A case shall not assign an error to the reporter merely because they opened the case.
Shared work may attribute different actions to different participants.
When attribution is unknown, learning should remain at team, case, or organizational level rather than invent individual responsibility.
Attribution confidence shall influence learning weight.
Patterns shall preserve sample size and contextual scope.
Correlation shall not automatically become causal knowledge.
Rare patterns shall remain low-confidence until sufficient support accumulates.
Pattern learning may generate candidate claims for review.

sequence_learning.description: ARIA shall learn not only which actions succeeded, but which diagnostic sequences produced efficient resolution.
rules: Sequence performance shall preserve context.
Shorter sequences are not automatically better if they carry greater risk or lower diagnostic reliability.
Sequence learning shall influence route selection, not create mandatory static troubleshooting trees.

causal_learning.description: ARIA may increase empirical causal confidence when validated interventions repeatedly produce predicted technical outcomes.
rules: Causal learning requires stronger evidence than correlation learning.
Multiple variables changed simultaneously shall reduce causal attribution confidence.
Before-and-after improvement alone does not guarantee causation when uncontrolled variables exist.
Repeated controlled observations may generate candidate canonical causal relationships.

canonical_knowledge_promotion.description: Experience-derived patterns may propose additions or changes to canonical knowledge but shall enter the provenance and review process.
rules: Repeated field correlation shall not automatically create CAN_CAUSE.
Experience may establish ASSOCIATED_WITH before sufficient causal evidence exists.
Manufacturer contradiction shall trigger review rather than silent overwrite.
Canonical promotion decisions shall remain auditable.

anti_poisoning.description: ARIA shall resist accumulation of incorrect learned beliefs from weak, duplicated, manipulated, or misattributed experience.
rules: Multiple copies of the same underlying incident shall not inflate learned frequency.
Cases with uncertain diagnosis shall not receive full causal learning weight.
Learning derived from invalidated evidence shall be recalculated.
Deliberately repeated claims shall not create artificial historical confidence.
Sudden extreme learned shifts shall be detectable and reviewable.
Duplicate detection may flag cases for review.
Linked duplicate cases shall not be counted as independent learning observations.
Cases describing genuinely separate recurrences shall remain distinct.
Recurrence after validated resolution shall reduce confidence in the completeness or durability of the previous correction.
Recurrence may reveal an incomplete root cause.
Time to recurrence shall be preserved.
Repeated recurrence may change route and corrective-action effectiveness statistics.
A recurrence shall not silently erase the original case outcome.

negative_learning.description: ARIA shall learn from paths that were unsuccessful, irrelevant, redundant, or excessively costly.
examples: Repeated configuration checks produced no useful evidence in this context.
Radio replacement frequently failed to resolve this symptom pattern.
Physical inspection was often unnecessary when a configuration export could discriminate the same hypotheses.
rules: Negative learning modifies route utility rather than prohibiting technically valid actions.
A historically poor action may become useful when new evidence or context changes.
Negative learning shall preserve context and sample size.

learning_decay.description: Predictive influence of some learned experience may decay while the underlying historical record remains unchanged.
rules: Decay affects predictive weighting, not deletion.
Decay behavior may differ by learning domain.
Revision changes may supersede time-based decay for product or firmware patterns.

aggregation.description: ARIA may maintain materialized aggregates for speed while preserving the Experience Ledger as the authoritative source.
aggregate_examples: failure frequency by product and symptom
failure frequency by user and scope
average resolution time by route sequence
rules: Aggregates shall be reproducible from underlying ledger events.
Aggregates may be rebuilt when models change.
Aggregates shall preserve effective sample size and confidence.
Aggregates shall not become the only surviving representation of experience.

required_capabilities: Explain why a case was or was not eligible for learning.
Identify which aggregates the case influenced.
Identify which user-specific experience was updated.
Identify any candidate canonical claims generated.
Recalculate learned statistics if a case is later invalidated.

example.case: Nokia UBT-T 18 GHz commissioning RSL discrepancy
updates: Increase weighted occurrence of Main/Diversity routing error for similar UBT-T commissioning cases.
Increase effectiveness of Compare Main/Diversity RSL for this symptom pattern.
Increase effectiveness of Verify Main/Diversity Routing after asymmetric Main/Diversity evidence.
Update applicable user experience only according to actual participant attribution.

semantic_rules.rule: ARIA shall learn from validated experience, not merely from conversation frequency.
Case closure does not automatically make a case suitable for causal learning.
Learning weight shall reflect the quality of the case.
The Experience Ledger is authoritative for historical learning events; aggregates are derived representations.
User-specific experience shall remain contextual and attributable.
ARIA shall allow users, products, procedures, and route effectiveness to change over time.
Historical patterns may affect future priors without becoming canonical technical truth.
Repeated experience may generate candidate knowledge claims but shall not bypass provenance and validation.
Failed diagnostic routes are valid learning data when they reveal what not to prioritize in similar contexts.
Duplicate or dependent cases shall not be treated as independent experience.
Learning derived from invalidated evidence shall be recalculated.
ARIA shall distinguish correlation learning from causal learning.
A high-frequency field pattern shall not silently override an applicable deterministic technical requirement.
Learning shall preserve the exact technical context required to interpret historical relevance.
ARIA shall prefer recalculable statistical experience over permanently encoded opaque model intuition.
Language-model outputs may identify candidate patterns but shall not independently mutate authoritative learned experience.
The system shall preserve enough history to explain how ARIA's current learned expectation developed.
Learning confidence and diagnostic confidence are separate. A correct diagnosis does not automatically mean the case is a clean learning example.
The goal of learning is improved future reasoning, not merely accumulation of more data.
ARIA shall never intentionally improve apparent accuracy by hiding, deleting, or excluding difficult cases except under explicit data-quality rules.
